html:
The resignation of Suharto on 21 May 1998, after 32 years as president of Indonesia, under the pressure of economic collapse and mass protest.

The Asian financial crisis wiped out much of the value of the rupiah. Prices of rice and fuel soared, and millions lost their jobs. Students led protests across the country, demanding reformasi, reform, and an end to corruption tied to the Suharto family.

On 12 May security forces shot dead four students at Trisakti University in Jakarta. Over the next days riots swept the capital and other cities. Mobs looted and burned shops and homes, many owned by Chinese Indonesians, and more than a thousand people died. Women were raped. Students then occupied the parliament building, and ministers and allies deserted Suharto.

He handed power to his vice president, B. J. Habibie. The Reformasi era that followed freed the press, allowed new parties, held free elections in 1999, gave the regions more power and let East Timor vote for independence. Indonesia became one of the largest democracies in the world.
sum: The resignation of Suharto on 21 May 1998, after 32 years as president of Indonesia, under the pressure of economic collapse and mass protest.
